title: A Nestorian Hermitage between Jericho and the Jordan
author: D. C. Baramki and St. H. Stephan
location_note: 60 m beyond km 42 of the Jericho - Allenby Bridge road; no map reference; placed by name (Jericho).
reading: full (text from the DjVu XML; the searchtext file was refused with HTTP 500)
notes: Mud-brick dwelling chamber and chapel with mosaic floor and Syriac inscription; found by a road repairer in Feb. 1933 and cleared. Chapel floor sump not coded (floor drain). Excavator dates the hermitage tentatively to about the 9th century from the inscription; Byzantine sherds over the site.

features.site: niche in the west wall of the dwelling chamber
features.subtype: group of objects (pottery pipe fragment, glazed bowl with cover, two glass lamps, bronze censer, chain, stone cup, sulphur) hidden behind a stone
features.period: hermitage tentatively about the ninth century (excavator, from the inscription)
features.quote: with a stone in front concealing them
